prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System advises only; incident command retains authority; no autonomous dispatch/control. Actors: Duty Detection Officer=Orion; Air Attack Supervisor=Redtail; County Emergency Liaison; Tanker Base Manager; Helitack Crew Leader; Drone Pilot Operator; fire/emergency/aviation/public-safety partners. Records require full names. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal=Emberhall (triage/context/advice/status; decisions/restrictions/searchable dismissals; dismissals yield no assignments/notifications); Horizon Ridge Drone Dock=Kestrel (launch/recovery/charging/shelter; maintenance controller produces threshold-triggered Battery Swap Ticket); Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine=Lantern (normalizes image/thermal/weather; traceable intelligence/advice); MesoWest Weather Fusion Node=Brindle (quality-checked weather, wind/visibility routing context; rule-triggered Wind Shift Bulletin); Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console=Marigold (active aviation lanes/status; aircraft/loading/mission data to Air Attack Supervisor/Tanker Base Manager); VHF Radio Gateway Repeater=Badger (voice/workstation bridge; command/air-to-ground/county paths; broadband-loss continuity; controlled recording/access). North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet; South Lookout Camera Mast produces Camera Cleaning Log; both inform smoke visibility; licensed-wireless video/cellular backup. Smoke Classifier Module supplies confidence/Ridge Shadow Mask. Crewline Mobile Tablet delivers command-released confirmed context/maps/updates to Helitack Crew Leader. East Retardant Loading Pump produces Retardant Batch Slip after metering/sealing; Tanker Base Manager coordinates East/West Retardant Loading Pump readiness before assignment acceptance and sequences aircraft availability. Drone Tasking Service prepares constrained verification tasks, lacks release authority, shall avoid active aviation lanes. Air Attack Supervisor deconflicts routes before launch; Drone Pilot Operator reviews constraints/safety. County Emergency Liaison handles dispatch/roads/evacuation/notifications, sends Drone Corridor Permit after jurisdiction review; constraints entered in portal before briefing. Temporary restrictions follow aviation chain; Airspace Restricted State requires authority acceptance; supervisor checks restrictions against analytics perimeter intelligence before asset release. Bridging preserves available speaker identity; failed routes require portal impairment marking, Orion acknowledgement/alternate-contact verification before new aviation messages. Mandatory: segmentation/time-sync/health/audits; timestamp/georeference/status/source/model/acknowledgement traceability. Authorized reviewers accept/reject/verify;

New part:
S096: The Smoke Classifier Module may be temporarily down-weighted by the Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine when observation quality is suspected to be degraded.
S097: The Helitack Crew Leader uses the Crewline Mobile Tablet to acknowledge air-to-ground instructions and report whether crews are inside any planned drop or reconnaissance area.
S098: The Caldera Incident Command Portal displays crew acknowledgements beside aviation tasks so the Air Attack Supervisor can verify that ground resources are clear before authorizing flight activity.
S099: If the Confirmed Ignition State is active and airspace approval is delayed, the system keeps suppression planning visible while preventing premature aircraft dispatch.
S100: Coordination records are retained with timestamps, participant identities, and radio path status so post-incident review can reconstruct both aviation decisions and interagency notifications.
S101: This section defines how the system converts detection observations, aerial imagery, weather updates, and geospatial overlays into a shared fire behavior assessment for operational use.
S102: The assessment begins when visual detections are correlated with incident geometry, terrain, fuel type, and current resource locations in the mapping workspace.
S103: North Lookout Camera Mast captures a time-stamped smoke column bearing and reports the pan, tilt, zoom, and confidence values needed to project the observation onto terrain.
S104: South Lookout Camera Mast supplies a separate bearing track so the mapping workflow can triangulate a probable origin area and bound the uncertainty ellipse.
S105: The Smoke Classifier Module assigns each observation a smoke likelihood, growth trend, and obscuration flag before the result is made available for analyst review.
S106: The Duty Detection Officer uses the spot snippet to compare the automated classification with visible flame, smoke color, and terrain context before accepting the observation into the assessment queue.
S107: Drone imagery is treated as a higher-resolution confirmation layer when weather, airspace, and communications conditions permit flight operations.
S108: The Drone Tasking Service packages approved imaging objectives as map footprints, altitude bands, and revisit intervals so the requested coverage can be compared with the active perimeter model.
S109: The Drone Pilot Operator uses the swap ticket to keep imaging sorties aligned with available aircraft endurance and expected return time.
S110: Frames collected during a sortie are orthorectified against the terrain model and registered to the incident grid before they are used for perimeter adjustment.
S111: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine identifies heat signatures, smoke edges, flame fronts, and potential spot fire indicators in the registered imagery.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
